meta.title: The Three Goats and the Bridge
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale with repeated lines

paragraphs: On Sunday afternoon, Grandpa sits in the garden with Tom and Lily. Pip lies on the grass next to Lily. "I will tell you an old tale," says Grandpa. "Move your hands like feet, and say the words with me." Tom and Lily laugh and hold up their hands. Grandpa smiles and starts the tale.

Once there were three goats. They wanted to cross a bridge to the green land. The bridge was old and noisy, and the water under it was deep. A wild bear lived under the bridge. He was enormous and furry, and he was unfriendly. The small goat went first. "Trip, trap, trip, trap!" went his feet. Suddenly, the bear put his big head up from under the bridge. He looked frightening. "Who is walking on my bridge?" asked the bear. "It is only me," said the small goat. "I am small, so please wait for my brother." "OK, go. I will wait for your brother," said the bear.

Then the second goat came. "Trip, trap, trip, trap!" went his feet. "Who is walking on my bridge?" asked the bear. "It is only me," said the second goat. "I am not big, so please wait for my brother." "OK, go. I will wait for your brother," said the bear. Last came the big goat. "Trip, trap, trip, trap!" went his feet, and the old bridge was very noisy. "Who is walking on my bridge?" shouted the bear. "I will not stop," said the big goat. "You are unhappy, but you are not kind. Go away!"

The bear tried to push the big goat off the bridge. But the big goat was strong, and he pushed back. The bear sat down on the grass. "I am sorry," he said. "I won't be unfriendly again." Then the goats and the bear ate grass together on the green land. Grandpa ends the tale, and Pip says, "Woof!" "Will the bear be kind now?" asks Tom. "Yes, he will," says Grandpa. "I like the big goat," says Lily.
text.summary: Grandpa tells Tom and Lily an old tale in the garden. Three goats want to cross a bridge, and a wild bear stops them. The big goat is strong, and the bear says sorry.
